study_identification_part.si4_title: Contrasting Case-Control and Normative Reference Approaches to Capture Clinically Relevant Structural Brain Abnormalities in Patients With First-Episode Psychosis Who Are Antipsychotic Naive

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Evaluate whether baseline deviations from a normative reference in subcortical volumes better predict antipsychotic treatment response than raw volumes in antipsychotic-naive first-episode psychosis (FEP).

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Normative model calibration using local healthy controls (n=92). The brain charts normative models were adapted to the University of Alabama at Birmingham site by learning site-specific effects from local healthy controls. During calibration, the lifespan trajectory shape remains unchanged, but scale and intercept are adjusted to fit the new site data.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: We used control data to calibrate normative curves. ... Normative models can be applied to new data sets. To transfer the normative models to new sites, healthy controls from the new data set are used to learn site effects. During calibration, the shape of the curve remains unchanged (because the life span trajectories of region-level brain volumes are the same, regardless of which scanner is used), but the scale and the intercept are adjusted to fit the new data set.

nm1_model_origin.detail: BrainCharts reference models trained on 58,836 healthy individuals across the lifespan (Rutherford et al., 2022), applied via PCNtoolkit/BrainCharts and calibrated to UAB controls following Dinga et al. (2021).
